NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Villagers want a group to watch over the river and set rules for cutting timber: form the group, or leave it to every family.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The river is muddier than it was, and the hills above it have been cut for timber. (subject) wants a group of guardians to watch the river and decide how much timber may be cut each season. (friend) says every family should look after its own part. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The river guardians are chosen and set rules: cut one tree, plant two. Some families grumble about being told what to do. In two years, the river runs clearer.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Every family looks after its own stretch. Some do it well, some do not. The river is clean in places and muddy in others. (friend) starts to think a few rules might help after all.
